biography.plain_text: Stavros Niarchos was a Greek shipowner who built one of the world's largest private tanker fleets. His entry into shipping grew from his maternal family's grain business, where he saw the savings in owning transport vessels. He expanded after the war, reinvesting insurance proceeds and financing new ships against long-term oil-company charters.

long_biography.plain_text:
Greek shipowner Stavros Niarchos assembled an art collection spanning Old Masters and modern French painting. His acquisitions included works by El Greco, Van Gogh and Picasso, and a substantial collection bought from the actor Edward G. Robinson. He also purchased much of the Puiforcat silver collection and donated it to the Louvre while retaining lifetime use.

His will extended that commitment to giving beyond individual works of art. A substantial bequest endowed the foundation bearing his name, which began making grants after his death. Its work covers education, health, social welfare, and arts and culture in Greece and internationally.
